# rpatch

> rpatch edits existing UTF-8 files by exact match, many edits across many files in one call, all or nothing. It replaces whole lines (OLD), part of a line (OLD part) or a range (FROM/TO), or inserts lines (BEFORE/AFTER). The input is a block format read from stdin, so nothing needs escaping. When an edit does not match, nothing is written and the error shows line numbers and the likely cause.

Run `rpatch --help`: a summary within 40 lines that covers everything needed to use it. `rpatch --help TOPIC` (blocks, json, rules, output) prints the details, `rpatch --help all` the whole text.

```sh
rpatch <<'EOF' && git diff --stat
=== path/to/file
<<<<<<< OLD
whole lines to replace, copied exactly (indentation included)
=======
replacement lines (empty to delete them)
>>>>>>> NEW
<<<<<<< OLD part
part of a line
=======
its replacement
>>>>>>> NEW
=== another/file
<<<<<<< AFTER
any part of the line to insert after
=======
inserted lines
>>>>>>> NEW
EOF
```

Key rules:

- OLD matches whole lines only, at line starts. For part of a line, use `<<<<<<< OLD part`.
- Each text must match exactly once (or `count=N` times, as in `<<<<<<< OLD count=2`). Overlapping matches are an error.
- Edits to one file apply in order; each sees the result of the previous one.
- Quote the heredoc delimiter (`<<'EOF'`). Chain follow-up commands on the opener line (`rpatch <<'EOF' && …`); a command on a line after the closing EOF runs even when the edit failed.
- `rpatch --probe CMD... <<'EOF' … EOF` breaks the files with the edits, runs CMD, always restores them byte for byte, and exits 0 if CMD failed (the break is caught) or 1 if it passed (not caught). `rpatch --help probe`.
- Exit status: 0 ok, 1 an edit did not match, a file is missing, or the file mixes LF and CRLF line endings, 2 invalid input, 3 I/O error.
- rpatch does not create or delete files and has no regular expressions.

## Docs

- [Design](docs/design.en.md): the processing flow, matching rules for each kind of edit, diagnostics, writing, and exit status.
- [Help text](src/help.txt): the whole text; `rpatch --help` prints its summary, `rpatch --help all` all of it.
- [MCP server](docs/mcp.md): optional, behind the Cargo feature `mcp` (Japanese).
